h1: De Lanna Hotel — A Lanna Boutique in the Heart of the Old City
intro: Picture this: a Lanna-roofed hotel tucked into a tropical garden inside the old city walls, a few minutes' walk from Tha Phae Gate, the ancient temples and the Sunday Walking Street — De Lanna Hotel is the boutique many travellers pick for its contemporary Thai feel and central location at a price well below the luxury hotels · Opened in 2009 · most of its 62 rooms have a private balcony, from approx. THB 1,400/night.

Contemporary Thai-style room with a wooden bed and a private balcony overlooking the garden
Lanna gabled-roof buildings of the hotel amid green trees in the Old City

body.html: De Lanna opened in 2009 and positions itself as a Lanna-style boutique hotel in the heart of the Chiang Mai Old City · What has kept it among the popular midrange choices for years is its location inside the old city walls on the Sri Phum side, an easy walk to Tha Phae Gate, the temples and the Sunday Walking Street · The hotel is a cluster of Lanna gabled-roof buildings around a tropical garden, and once you step off the street it's quieter and leafier than you'd expect — many reviews describe it as a small oasis in the middle of a busy quarter.

There are 62 rooms, from the roughly 25 sq m Superior up to the 48 sq m Honeymoon King Suite · The thing guests mention often is that most rooms have a private balcony looking onto the garden or pool — a spot to rest after a full day of sightseeing that many love · Rooms are done in contemporary Thai style with wooden beds and Lanna textiles, and come with air conditioning, a safe and free Wi-Fi · To be honest though, the hotel has been open since 2009, and some reviews warn that the rooms show signs of wear and the bathrooms are on the small side.
"Sitting on the balcony in the evening after a whole day of temple-walking, looking down at the garden pool — so quiet and relaxing, even though Tha Phae Gate is just minutes away."

At the centre of the hotel is the outdoor pool set in a tropical garden, which many reviews call a highlight — cool water, shaded by trees, perfect for a dip to beat the heat after a day out · There's a poolside bar, a small gym and an in-hotel restaurant · The buffet breakfast draws consistent praise, with both Thai and international dishes made from local ingredients, served in a pleasant garden setting.

Service is another point reviews agree on · Many staff are described as warm and helpful — sorting out car hire, tours and restaurant recommendations · There's a 24-hour front desk, airport transfers, and rental cars and bicycles for getting around the Old City · The overall feel is a mid-size hotel built around comfort and location rather than luxury, well suited to travellers who plan to spend most of their time out exploring.

The honest trade-offs from real guest reviews are the age of the rooms and inconsistent hot water · Several reviews note showers that sometimes aren't warm enough and weak water pressure, plus older air-conditioning units that can be noisy at night · Some bathrooms feel cramped for two · If you expect a brand-new room or a 5-star spa, this isn't it — but viewed as a well-located room at an affordable price, most guests call it good value.

The overall score sits at 8.7 from 166 reviews on Trip.com, and 4.0/5 on TripAdvisor from 786 reviews, ranking mid-table among Chiang Mai hotels · Its highest-scoring point is the location, which earns a perfect 100/100 walk score · Those numbers reflect that most guests are happy with the setting and value, while most complaints come down to the age of the rooms.

The verdict from real guest reviews: De Lanna is best for travellers who want to stay in the heart of the Old City, walk to the temples and the Walking Street, at an affordable price · If you plan to be out all day and just want a clean room, a great location, and a pool for an evening dip — and you're not fussy about a brand-new room — this delivers · But if you want a fully modern room or the full facilities of a luxury hotel, you may want to look a tier up in another area.

honestSummary: De Lanna Hotel is the best choice for travellers who want a heart-of-the-Old-City location, walkable temples and Walking Street, and a garden pool, all at an affordable price · The honest trade-offs are rooms that are starting to age, inconsistent hot water, and bathrooms on the small side.
honestChecks: If you expect a brand-new room with full facilities — the hotel opened in 2009, rooms show some wear and hot water can be inconsistent → if that bothers you, choose a recently renovated hotel.
If you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise — older AC units and noise from neighbouring rooms can disturb some rooms → request a recently updated or quieter-floor room when you book.
If you're travelling with lots of luggage or as a couple who want a roomy bathroom — some bathrooms are cramped → choose a Deluxe or Suite with more space.

tips.title: Make the most of the location
tips.body: Tha Phae Gate, Wat Chedi Luang and the Sunday Walking Street are all walkable — no need to call a Grab often, which saves both time and money.

tips.title: Ask for a recently updated room
tips.body: The hotel has been open for years and rooms vary — request a renovated room or a quieter floor when you book to get one in better condition.

tips.title: Take an evening dip
tips.body: The garden pool is quiet and shaded in the evening — ideal after a full day out, and you can order a drink at the poolside bar.

tips.title: Book ahead in high season
tips.body: November–February and the Yi Peng festival fill up fast — compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com and lock in a free-cancellation rate first.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — De Lanna Hotel Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is De Lanna Hotel, and what's nearby?
faq.a: De Lanna is at 44 Intrawarorot Road, Sri Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, inside the old city walls · It's about a 7-minute walk to Tha Phae Gate and 8 minutes to Wat Chedi Luang, with the Sunday Walking Street very close · The Night Bazaar and Chiang Mai Airport are about 12–15 minutes by car.

faq.q: How much does De Lanna Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 1,400/night for a Superior Room of about 25 sq m · Larger options include the Deluxe Room (~30 sq m) and the Honeymoon King Suite (48 sq m) · Most rooms have a private balcony · High-season rates climb, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is De Lanna Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who want to stay in the heart of the Old City, walk to the temples and the Walking Street, at an affordable price · Good for couples, solo travellers or families who value location and value over luxury · It's not the choice for those who need a brand-new room or full 5-star facilities.

faq.q: Does De Lanna Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes · There's an outdoor pool set in a tropical garden with a poolside bar and a leafy, relaxing feel · Breakfast is a buffet with both Thai and international dishes from local ingredients, served in the garden · Some rates include breakfast, so check when you book.

faq.q: What are the downsides to know before booking De Lanna Hotel?
faq.a: The most common complaints in reviews are that the rooms are starting to age since it opened in 2009, hot water can be inconsistent, and some bathrooms are small · A few rooms pick up older AC noise or sound from neighbours · If that matters, request a recently updated room or a higher room category when you book.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: For high season (November–February) and the Yi Peng / Loy Krathong festival, rooms fill up fast — book 1–2 months ahead · Other times, 2–3 weeks is usually enough · Every platform offers a free-cancellation option — pick that if your plans aren't firm yet.
